baseline_models.mechanism: A dispatched event bounded to one frightening cry is followed by fa- and the plural's entry into a shattered material state. The singular cause/plural result asymmetry makes sufficiency, not duration, the force of the line.

activation_trace.role: Dispatch and release present the cry as an emitted causal agent rather than a mere report.
The frightening cry supplies a sudden harmful acoustic event.
Numerical oneness bounds the cause to one event and sharpens its asymmetry with the plural victims.
Occurrence in time carries the plural into the resulting state after fa-.
Dry broken vegetation supplies the resulting material condition of fragmentation.

changed_reading.before: A loud punishment destroys the group.
changed_reading.after: One bounded dispatch is shown sufficient to convert a plural collective immediately into fragment-like matter.

baseline_models.mechanism: The simile couples vegetation already dry and broken with an enclosure that gathers and blocks. Destruction is therefore pictured not as disappearance but as the loose remains associated with a containing boundary.

activation_trace.role: Dry vegetation broken small supplies the residue rather than a merely dead plant.
A barrier that both gathers and blocks supplies the prior logic of containment whose brushwood remains.
Breaking and crushing make the enclosure material's loss of integrity functional in the simile.

changed_reading.before: They are compared generically to dry straw.
changed_reading.after: They resemble the broken residue of a boundary-making structure: a bounded collective rendered loose and structurally useless.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier episode repeats the 'We sent upon them' frame with wind as payload, then shows people uprooted as palm rears. The focus substitutes a cry and ends with broken brushwood, so the parallel makes sound operate as transmitted force and advances the material image from whole uprooted trunks to small fragments.

activation_trace.role: The same dispatch and release branch establishes a causal frame shared with the focus.
Wind and moving air supply the earlier dispatched physical medium.
Pulling a thing from its fixed place supplies the first scene's destructive action.
The palm tree supplies a large intact comparison-object before the focus shifts scale to brush fragments.
Uprooting from the base completes the earlier whole-trunk image.
The high sound occupies the same payload slot that wind occupied in the parallel dispatch.
Broken dry vegetation marks a finer terminal material state than the uprooted palms.

structural_cues: 54:19 and 54:31 repeat إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ with only the dispatched payload changed.
54:20 and 54:31 both close destruction with plant-material similes at different scales.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated dispatch syntax, wind, uprooting, palms, cry, and broken brush; I infer a medium-to-force analogy and progressive comminution. A live alternative is that the scenes are only rhetorical parallels and imply no shared physical mechanics.

changed_reading.before: The cry is an acoustic signal followed by an unrelated debris simile.
changed_reading.after: The cry takes the earlier wind's causal slot as a transmitted force, with the two episodes moving from uprooted trunks to comminuted enclosure brush.

context_deltas.mechanism: The group objects to following one human from among themselves; a sent she-camel then serves as their test; finally one sent cry is sufficient for the whole group. Repeated oneness and sending turn their contempt for a singular bearer into the exact economy of the response.

activation_trace.role: The visible-skinned human supplies the ordinary human bearer whom they reject.
One in number marks the singleness they make objectionable.
Following behind supplies the rejected relation to that one human.
A prior act of sending places the she-camel in the sequence of dispatched interventions.
Testing a person or metal makes the sent she-camel the probationary phase before judgment.
The focus repeats dispatch but changes the sent intervention from test to destructive cry.
The frightening cry is the final dispatched term in the reversal.
One in number returns as the sufficient measure of the response.

structural_cues: 54:24 and 54:31 place forms of وَاحِد directly after the contested or dispatched entity.
54:27 repeats the sending construction between the two occurrences of oneness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies one human, rejected following, a sent test, and one sent cry; I infer a measured rhetorical reversal from rejected singularity to sufficient singularity. The alternative is that both uses of 'one' are locally quantitative without a designed answer relation.

changed_reading.before: One cry only emphasizes the event's brevity or power.
changed_reading.after: One cry also answers the group's contempt for following one human: the singularity they rejected returns as all that is needed to undo the plural group.

context_deltas.mechanism: The group raises a call to its companion, who undertakes the act and hamstrings the animal; after the refrain, one high cry acts upon the entire group. Sound initiates action in both directions, while agency reverses from a collective mobilizing one member to one cry collapsing the collective.

activation_trace.role: Raising the voice and calling supplies the group's initiating sound.
Companionship identifies the one actor as socially continuous with the calling group.
Undertaking and entering an act converts the group's call into individual agency.
Hamstringing the animal supplies the disabling act produced by the first call.
A high sound supplies the answering acoustic event that now produces action upon the callers.
One in number reverses the prior collective-to-individual agency pattern.

structural_cues: 54:29 sequences collective call, companion, undertaking, and disabling act.
54:30 interrupts with the punishment-warning refrain before 54:31 sequences cry and collective collapse.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two sound-to-action sequences and opposite one/group directions; I infer a call/counter-call architecture. A live alternative is ordinary chronological succession without reciprocal design.

changed_reading.before: The cry is a unilateral destructive noise.
changed_reading.after: The cry functions as a counter-call: their call mobilized one companion against the sign, while one answering cry acts against all of them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The water arrangement separates a share among parties and requires every drinking turn to be present or attended. The focus's enclosure then supplies a material analogue for bounded allocation, while its broken dry contents render that ordering structure as residue after breach.

activation_trace.role: Division and assignment of a portion supply the regulated resource boundary.
Separation and differentiation distribute the water arrangement among distinct parties.
Comprehensive totality makes the allocation rule apply to every drinking turn.
A share of water supplies the concrete unit being bounded and alternated.
Presence, witnessing, and nearness make each share an attended appointment rather than unregulated access.
The enclosure's gathering barrier materializes the context's system of bounded access.
Broken dry vegetation turns the bounded system into loose residue.

structural_cues: 54:28 clusters division, among-ness, every share, and attendance immediately before the collective breach in 54:29.
54:31 ends with the paired material roots for broken vegetation and enclosure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an allocated water order and a later enclosure-debris image; I infer that physical containment becomes an analogue for social allocation and its collapse. The alternative keeps the enclosure wholly concrete and unrelated to the water rule.

changed_reading.before: The enclosure detail only localizes the kind of straw in the simile.
changed_reading.after: The broken enclosure material also mirrors a community that would not sustain bounded shares: ordered separation ends as undifferentiated residue.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding refrain asks how punishment and warning 'was'; the focus answers with fa-'they became' and a visible material state; the next refrain opens the Qur'an to remembrance. The ayah is therefore a hinge that converts an evaluative question into an image made available for recollection.

activation_trace.role: Occurrence in time frames the preceding question about how punishment came to be.
Warning that frightens and awakens caution sets the prospective function of the result.
The repeated being-event root shifts from the question to the victims' resulting state.
Broken dry vegetation gives the answer a compact visible form.
Opening and ease after difficulty supply the accessibility frame immediately after the image.
Reminder and what causes remembering make the debris image available as a caution-bearing mnemonic.

structural_cues: 54:30 asks فَكَيْفَ كَانَ and 54:31 answers with فَكَانُوا.
54:31 is enclosed between the punishment-warning refrain and the ease-remembrance refrain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated k-w-n hinge and the warning and remembrance frames; I infer that the material result functions as their mnemonic conversion point. A live alternative is that 54:32 addresses the Qur'an generally without assigning this image a special mnemonic role.

changed_reading.before: The ayah is the terminal punishment image of the episode.
changed_reading.after: The ayah answers the refrain's 'how' by making the result visible, then hands that visible state forward as material for warning-remembrance.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the sounding-fracture branch is secondary to the ordinary high or frightening cry. It remains anchored by صَيْحَة beside هَشِيم's literal breaking and by the single-event causal syntax; downstream prose should render it only as an acoustic-material overlay, not replace 'cry' with 'crack.'

activation_trace.role: Sound-producing splitting lets the acoustic event carry a latent image of fissure.
One in number compresses the possible fissure into a single rupture-pulse.
Breaking and crushing provide the material completion of the acoustic fissure image.

changed_reading.before: The cry happens first and physical breakage follows as a separate effect.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the single cry and the shattered result can be heard as two registers of one rupture: fracture sounding and sound materialized.

strongest_changes: The earlier wind and uprooted-palms parallel makes the cry act as a transmitted force and advances the material image from trunks to fragments.
The rejected one human and the group's call to one companion are reversed by one cry acting upon the whole group.
The divided-water order activates the enclosure as a bounded system reduced to residue, while 54:30-32 converts the result into warning-memory.
summary.what_was_special: The focus's singular/plural asymmetry, the ه ش م-ح ظ ر material coupling, and the local repetition of sending, oneness, calling, and ك و ن produced causal and social reversals rather than a generic destruction theme.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the ص ي ح sounding-fracture branch supports a real acoustic-material overlay or only a distant lexicographic resonance.
How far the resource-boundary model may move beyond the concrete enclosure simile.
The wind parallel establishes rhetorical mechanics but does not prove an identical physical medium.
